text:
marcos: Heads-up — support flagged a customer who saw a provisional charge stick around and then a confirmed charge after a region fallback. user says stream reconnected twice.

tess: Can you paste the ledger lines?

marcos: here: `2024-06-02T10:12:22Z provisional session=xyz789 bt=bt-a1` then `2024-06-02T10:12:24Z confirm session=xyz789 bt=bt-b2`

anya: is session id preserved across the reconnect? we switched to server-session canonicalization last quarter, but some clients still send session_id.

marcos: user sent this: `session=xyz789 client_session=xyz789-legacy resume_token=rT_44 toolcall=true truncated_prefix=1`

billing-bot: Ledger note: provisional and confirm have different `billing_trace` and `route_region` (us-east vs eu-west). No explicit dedupe linkage recorded.

tess: suspected flow: provisional recorded on initial route, then fallback creates a new trace because resume_token didn't map or prefix metadata changed due to truncation during active toolcall.

anya: unfortunate combo: toolcalls may rewrite prefix when we inject tool output, and our dedupe key is prefix-hash + session. truncation toggles that hash.

marcos: repro idea: start a toolcall stream, emit a tool chunk that causes server-side truncation, then kill primary, force fallback. I can try netem + route-force.

anya: quick mitigation options: 1) Router: when accepting resume_token, try to match provisional traces by session OR by fallback of prefix-less session mapping. 2) Billing: delay confirm by 200ms on fallback if there exists a provisional in last 5s for same session. 3) Console: show provisional traces in session timeline and surface `billing_trace` to support.

tess: console change seems low-risk and high-value. support can immediately see if a confirm is a separate trace. add a provisional badge.

marcos: agree. for routing fix, prefer deterministic server-side session mapping rather than relying on client session. if sidecar adds resume_token it should include `canonical_session_id` and `toolcall_checksum` so fallback can match.

billing-bot: Metric: increased `fallback_confirm_mismatch_count` observed from 0 -> 8/day for last 2 days. emitting alert to #eng-oncall.

anya: Implementation notes for router patch: - extend resume token payload: canonical_session_id (uuid), toolcall_checksum (sha1), last_prefix_hash (nullable). - fallback broker: lookup order: 1) canonical_session_id -> existing trace, 2) toolcall_checksum + session -> best match, 3) last_prefix_hash if present. If none -> new trace.

marcos: Need to be careful: checksum comparison must tolerate truncation; maybe use prefix similarity threshold rather than exact match. That adds complexity.

tess: For short term enact option 2 (billing delay) plus console change. document tradeoffs in RFC.

anya: I'll draft the router patch PR and unit tests focused on toolcall truncation. mark feature-flag behind `resume_strict_match=false` toggle so we can roll out gradually.

marcos: I'll own the console ticket — adding billing_trace column + provisional coloring. Also add a quick link to ledger entries.

console-bot: Created console task CONS-4123 (show billing_trace + provisional state).

billing-bot: Created billing task BILL-909 (defer confirm on fallback when provisional exists within 5s).

marcos: Thanks. Next sync: Friday incident review if rate doesn't drop after patch.

tess: TY everyone. small ask: include sample logs in PR description (resume_token, traces) so oncall can reason quickly. :thumbsup:
